passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 202 Academic Writing 2: Genre & Structure Across Disciplines (2 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 202 Academic Writing 2: Genre & Structure Across Disciplines (2 credits)
passages.text: Prerequisite(s): Must complete WOC 201 (Academic Writing 1: Argumentation Across Disciplines) with a grade of B or higher.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 205 Writing about Endangered Languages (4 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 205 Writing about Endangered Languages (4 credits)
passages.text: Through study of endangered languages, this course will help students improve their ability to research an issue by using library resources in multiple languages, and to write a well-grounded and persuasive course paper in which students make a case for their position on this issue; students will also improve their ability to make their case through a well-informed and persuasive oral presentation. Last but not least, through study of this issue, students will learn more about the role of languages in today’s globalizing world.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 206 Debating Scenarios for Sustainable Futures (2 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 206 Debating Scenarios for Sustainable Futures (2 credits)
passages.text: This course will focus on the fundamentals of argumentation, refutation, and value and impact analysis. Rather than allowing debates to end with a winner, however, students will also explore the importance of reconciliation with consensus-building tasks that generate alternative solutions by considering all stakeholder perspectives and suggesting amicable resolutions to these debates.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 207/CHINESE 408 Translation Workshop – Chinese/English English/Chinese (2 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 207/CHINESE 408 Translation Workshop – Chinese/English English/Chinese (2 credits)
passages.text: This class is a practical introduction to the art of written translation for students with advanced proficiency in both Chinese and English. Its goal is to give students hands-on experience translating a variety of interesting and challenging texts between Chinese and English, thereby honing their skills as readers and writers of both languages while also probing deeper philosophical questions about how translation works.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 207/CHINESE 408 Translation Workshop – Chinese/English English/Chinese (2 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 207/CHINESE 408 Translation Workshop – Chinese/English English/Chinese (2 credits)
passages.text: Prerequisite(s): EAP-track students must have completed EAP 102B or have Consent of the Instructor. CSL-track students must have completed or placed out of CHINESE 402B.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 208 An Introduction to Language Teaching (2 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 208 An Introduction to Language Teaching (2 credits)
passages.text: This course introduces the key components of language teaching to students who have an interest in teaching languages and who may wish to engage in language teaching assignments either during or after their DKU studies. Based on the Cambridge English Teaching Framework and using English as the main language of focus, the course is rooted in pedagogical theory focusing on practical knowledge and teaching skills that can be easily applied to the teaching of various languages (i.e., not only teaching English). The primary objective of the course is to build students’ awareness of what effective language teaching is and to equip them with the essential skills needed to start teaching.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 209 Intercultural Communication and Advertising – Persuasion Across Cultures (2 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 209 Intercultural Communication and Advertising – Persuasion Across Cultures (2 credits)
passages.text: This course explores Hofstede’s cultural dimensions and their application to the world of international advertising to help students to develop their academic oral and written English analysis skills. Specifically, students will learn how to construct professional and persuasive oral and written analyses through analyzing multiple international advertising case studies through a critical lens. The course explores how Hofstede’s cultural dimensions can help us to understand the rhetorical moves used by the media in the world of advertising, enabling students to apply theory to practice whilst developing critical thinking skills. Academic oral and written English skills will also be developed through creative and engaging assignments.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 211 Composing Research 1: Developing a Research Proposal (2 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 211 Composing Research 1: Developing a Research Proposal (2 credits)
passages.text: WOC 211 aims at preparing students for their signature work at DKU and similar projects. This research preparedness course will engage students with writing on the research process and guide them in producing a research proposal on their chosen topics. Students will search for and evaluate relevant literature, store and manage references, frame the research question(s), and determine research approaches. Students will develop their critical thinking, problem-solving, teamwork, and communication skills during the research proposal writing process. These learning modules will help students learn how to engage in academic conversations and contribute to the existing literature.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 212 Composing Research 2: Developing a Research Paper (2 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 212 Composing Research 2: Developing a Research Paper (2 credits)
passages.text: WOC 212 continues to prepare students for their signature work at DKU and similar projects. This course will guide students in conducting their proposed research and developing a preliminary research paper. Students will do writing assignments in which they analyze data, assess data's validity and reliability, report findings based on research questions, and discuss their findings in light of other relevant studies. Through these writing assignments, students will build a foundation of knowledge on a topic, practice collecting and analyzing data, learn how to answer research questions by reporting their results and discussing their findings, and familiarize themselves with the academic research process.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 212 Composing Research 2: Developing a Research Paper (2 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 212 Composing Research 2: Developing a Research Paper (2 credits)
passages.text: Prerequisite(s): WOC 211 Composing Research 1. Students who have had a research proposal that is ready for implementation but have not taken Composing Research 1 are also welcome to take this course.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 213 From Text to World: Editing and Publishing (2 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 213 From Text to World: Editing and Publishing (2 credits)
passages.text: In this course students will learn the fundamentals of editing while working together to produce a publication (anthology or journal/magazine issue) that showcases the talents of DKU's student writers. Students will learn how to give more effective feedback, edit for style and content, and consider texts from a potential reader's perspective, while following the journey of a written text from the writer's conception to the editors' curation and finally into print. Each student will undertake an independent writing project upon which they will practice the editing and revision skills we learn in this class. Students are encouraged to contact the instructor in advance to learn about the publication's theme for a given session and to discuss their potential independent project.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 216 Introduction to Feature Writing and International Reporting (2 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 216 Introduction to Feature Writing and International Reporting (2 credits)
passages.text: This course will focus on reporting and writing about societal trends, human interest stories, and cultural changes in China – all through the lens of international affairs. Students will pitch, report, write, and edit two original feature stories about issues and trends at DKU or beyond over the session; their best story will then be revised for website publication. We will also explore how international correspondents provide coverage of global or local issues in a foreign country for a worldwide audience and examine some of the best international reporting from the last 30 years – from “legacy” media outlets like the New York Times, to cutting-edge new media outlets like Buzzfeed.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 217 Introduction to News Writing (2 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 217 Introduction to News Writing (2 credits)
passages.text: This course will develop students’ abilities to report and write their own original news stories about timely events at DKU or beyond. Students will pitch, report, write, and edit two original news stories over the session; their best story will then be revised for website publication. The course will also focus on ethics and best practices issues in journalism: What are the effects when journalism functions at its best, and “shines a light in the darkness,” or provides a “voice to the voiceless” in society? What happens when reporters fabricate, and betray the public trust? We will also examine how to make distinctions among propaganda, publicity & public relations, and actual credible journalism.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 218 Public Speaking (2 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 218 Public Speaking (2 credits)
passages.text: In Public Speaking students will learn to understand and interpret public communication processes and practice skills needed for communicating and functioning in a variety of real-life situations. In this course, students will build solid skills that will allow them to organize and express ideas in public settings confidently. Students will also learn how speech is closely tied to self and society.
passages.section_id: Part 10: Majors and Courses / Course Descriptions

passages.subsection: Courses with Course Subject: Written and Oral Communication (WOC) / WOC 290 Special Topics in Written and Oral Communication (4 credits)
passages.heading: WOC 290 Special Topics in Written and Oral Communication (4 credits)
passages.text: This is a theme-based writing seminar course that has an emphasis on cross-cultural inquiry. It provides guided practice in intellectual reading and writing of the sort expected in courses across the academy and in civic and professional life beyond the university. The specific theme of the course will vary according to instructor. This course may be repeated for credit if the course content of the two courses is different.

findings.question: 1. What are the major semantic topics?
findings.answer: The largest groups are Credit, Placement & Curriculum Requirements (166 passages); Economics, Public Policy & Social Research (165 passages); Global History, Politics & Culture (151 passages). Additional topics distinguish language learning, degree rules, academic status, and catalog revisions. Representative passages and terms for all twelve groups are available above.

findings.question: 2. Which topics cross formal sections?
findings.answer: Degree Administration, Transfer & Student Services spans 9 formal section keys, including Study Away, Transfer of Work Taken Elsewhere, and Degree Requirements. This spread connects mobility and degree policies that the Bulletin presents in separate locations.

findings.question: 3. Which sections are most semantically diverse?
findings.answer: Among sections with at least ten passages, Course Descriptions contains 10 topics in 789 passages (Shannon entropy 2.94 bits); Majors (listed in alphabetical order) contains 10 topics in 124 passages (2.81 bits). Larger sections have more opportunities to contain multiple topics, so diversity should be interpreted with sample size.

findings.question: 4. Which passages from different sections are semantically similar?
findings.answer: A Degree Requirements paragraph describing the three Common Core courses and a Common Core Courses policy paragraph are semantic neighbors (cosine similarity 0.840). They discuss the same sequence from curricular and procedural perspectives.

findings.question: 5. Which passage is unusual relative to its section?
findings.answer: Within Degree Requirements, the paragraph about attaining proficiency in Chinese is one of only two passages assigned to Language Learning & Communication (two of 36 passages). Its emphasis on language competence connects it to language instruction elsewhere. This is a useful semantic contrast, not evidence of incorrect placement.

findings.question: 6. Are the search concepts concentrated or dispersed?
findings.answer: “credit” matches 158 passages across 10 topics and 30 formal sections; “graduation” matches 36 passages across 4 topics and 21 formal sections; “registration” matches 13 passages across 6 topics and 11 formal sections; “academic integrity” matches 5 passages across 5 topics and 4 formal sections. These are case-insensitive substring matches in passage text; “credit” also matches “credits” and “accredited”.
